Jordan — great questions. Quick answers and a proposed concrete test plan so we can scope the POC: 

Competitive differentiators vs hyperscaler endpoints: 
- Tracing & observability: we provide request-level traces plus KV/prefix visibility and correlate traces with token-level cost. Hyperscalers expose metrics but often lack first-class token-cost attribution and per-route dashboards focused on inference economics.
- Cost predictability: Redwood supports dedicated pools and routing policies (dedicated/dynamic/burst) and offers recommendations around batching/quantization that materially lower unit cost.
- Operational tooling: per-model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, automatic regression alerts tied to prompt sets, and exportable traces for integration into your APM.
- Fallbacks & reliability: automated routing to compatible model variants and region failover to preserve availability under capacity pressure.

Proposed POC tests (we can run these in parallel across a small dataset):
1) Latency test: single-request p95 at 512 tokens (target <250ms) — compare Redwood dedicated pool vs Bedrock/Vertex baseline.
2) Throughput test: sustained throughput with batching (simulate 100 concurrent users) and measure cost per 1M tokens.
3) Observability integration: send spans/traces to your APM (or review via our dashboard), validate request-level troubleshooting and alerting on regression.

Pre-reqs and operational notes: 
- Network/data: POC can run over the public API (TLS) or via an IP allowlist if you prefer. No customer data will be stored beyond ephemeral caching unless you opt in.
- We’ll provide a test harness (script + Docker) to simulate traffic and collect traces — SE (Dev) will own that.

I’ve attached a short demo notes doc and the mutual action plan to the thread. If you’re good with the scope I’ll schedule the kickoff and loop in Dev for the test harness.

Best,
Marissa
